current_definition: A conclusion or result that follows naturally and directly from something already proved or established, requiring little additional argument.
To confirm or support a claim, theory, or finding with independent evidence that points to the same conclusion.
To reach a specific conclusion by applying general principles or established facts in a logical, step-by-step way.
Based on direct observation, experiment, or measured data rather than on theory, tradition, or assumption alone.
To extend known data or a trend beyond the observed range in order to estimate what is likely to hold in new or future cases.
Involving a situation or scenario that is imagined rather than real, used as a basis for reasoning or testing an argument.
To draw a probable conclusion from specific evidence or observations, without that conclusion being directly stated or proved.
To put forward a claim or assumption as a starting point for reasoning or further investigation, without yet proving it.
A statement or assumption that is accepted as a starting point from which a conclusion is then drawn through reasoning.
The combination of separate ideas, findings, or elements into a single coherent whole that is more complete than any individual part.
Smugly or pointlessly foolish; showing a lack of intelligence or good judgment in a way that the speaker seems unaware of.
Lacking any sense, significance, or intelligent content; completely empty of meaning or value.
Out of place or inconsistent with the surrounding context; not fitting together in a natural or logical way.
So vague, unclear, or loosely formed that it is difficult to grasp or pin down; lacking definite shape or content.
Annoyingly slow to understand; lacking sharpness of intellect.
Repeating information that has already been clearly stated, adding nothing new.
Describing a statement that is true only because it repeats the same idea in different words, giving the appearance of reasoning without actually proving anything.
A short, memorable statement that expresses a general truth or clever observation about life.
A statement accepted as obviously true without proof, used as a starting point for further reasoning.
A formal or authoritative statement of a principle or opinion, especially one made by a judge, expert, or institution.
To be a perfect or typical example of something; to illustrate a concept by providing a clear example.
A short, widely accepted rule or piece of advice about how to behave or live well.
An experienced person who gives guidance, advice, and support to someone less experienced over a period of time.
New and original in a way that has not been seen or thought of before.
A typical example or model that represents a broader system of ideas, beliefs, or methods accepted by a community at a given time.
A general rule or principle intended to guide thought, behaviour, or moral conduct.
Most noticeable, important, or relevant among the features of something; standing out clearly.
A reliable standard or test by which the quality, value, or truth of something is judged.
An imagined place or society that is perfect in every respect, especially in its laws, politics, and social conditions.
Difficult to understand because it requires specialised knowledge or very deep thinking; not accessible to a general audience.
Known or understood by very few people; requiring secret or specialised knowledge that has not been widely shared.
Having a hidden or puzzling meaning that is difficult to interpret; deliberately brief and unclear.
A person, thing, or situation that is deeply puzzling and very difficult to understand or explain.
Intended for or understood by only a small group of people with specialised knowledge or interest; not for general audiences.
Not allowing liquid, light, or another substance to pass through; physically sealed against penetration.
Present but not yet visible, active, or developed; existing in a hidden or dormant state.
Not known to many people; difficult to find or little discussed, especially because it has been neglected or forgotten.
Not allowing light to pass through; not transparent or clear as a physical material.
A detailed written record of events arranged in the order in which they happened.
Relating to the mental processes involved in gaining knowledge, such as thinking, remembering, reasoning, and understanding.
Fully aware of and attentive to a fact or situation, especially one that requires careful consideration.
A thorough but concise collection of information on a subject, often drawn from many sources and arranged for easy reference.
Covering all or nearly all aspects of a subject; thorough enough that little or nothing important is left out.
Examining every possibility, element, or case with great thoroughness; leaving nothing out.
To be formally enrolled as a student at a university or college, marking official entry into a degree programme.
Relating to the nature, characteristics, or qualities of something rather than to numbers or measurable quantities.
Dealing with very specialised or little-known information that requires deep study to understand; known to very few experts.
Relating to the physical senses—sight, hearing, touch, taste, and smell—and the information they deliver to the brain.
Able to have subjective experiences and feelings; capable of perceiving and responding to one's environment in a conscious way.
Existing as a permanent and inseparable part of something; built into its very nature rather than added from outside.
